requirements.item_text: Self-inspections review ongoing compliance with the company's data governance policy and procedures to confirm they remain effective.

mappings.quote: Ongoing compliance with the company's data governance policy/procedures should be reviewed during self-inspection, to ensure that they remain effective.

requirements.item_text: The data integrity self-inspection may also cover elements of the data lifecycle (Q3-Q9).

mappings.quote: This may also include elements of the Data lifecycle discussed in Q3-Q9.

requirements.item_text: The data governance system ensures data lifecycle controls proportionate to quality risk management principles.

mappings.quote: The data governance system should ensure controls over the data lifecycle which are commensurate with the principles of quality risk management.

requirements.item_text: Data lifecycle controls may include organisational measures (procedures for completing and retaining records, staff training and documented authorisation for generating and approving data, governance system design that controls risks across how data is generated, recorded, processed, retained and used, routine data verification such as daily, batch- or activity-related checks, periodic surveillance such as self-inspection, and staff with data integrity and security expertise) and technical measures (computerised system validation, qualification and control, automation, or technologies giving greater data control).

mappings.quote: These controls may be:  Organisational o procedures, e.g. instructions for completion of records and retention of completed records; o training of staff and documented authorisation for data generation and approval; o data governance system design, considering how data is generated, recorded, processed, retained and used, and risks or vulnerabilities are controlled effectively; o routine (e.g. daily, batch- or activity-related) data verification; o periodic surveillance, e.g. self-inspection processes seek to verify the effectiveness of the data governance system; or o the use of personnel with expertise in data management and integrity, including expertise in data security measures.  Technical o computerised system validation, qualification and control; o automation; or o the use of technologies that provide greater controls for data management and integrity.

requirements.item_text: The effectiveness of data integrity controls is assessed periodically through self-inspection (internal audit) or other periodic reviews, to confirm that data lifecycle controls work as intended.

mappings.quote: The effectiveness of data integrity control measures should be assessed periodically as part of self-inspection (internal audit) or other periodic review processes. This should ensure that controls over the data lifecycle are operating as intended.

requirements.item_text: Self-inspections include a risk-based sample of computerised system logs and audit trails to confirm GMP/GDP-relevant information is reported accurately, particularly where routine system data is reviewed manually or through a validated exception report.

mappings.quote: A risk-based sample of computerised system logs / audit trails to ensure that information of relevance to GMP/GDP activity is reported accurately. This is relevant to situations where routine computerised system data is reviewed manually or by a validated ‘exception report’

requirements.item_text: The pharmaceutical quality system can prevent, detect and correct weaknesses in systems or processes that could lead to data integrity lapses.

mappings.quote: The company’s Pharmaceutical Quality System should be able to prevent, detect and correct weaknesses in the system or their processes that may lead to data integrity lapses.

requirements.item_text: The company knows its data lifecycle and builds in suitable controls and procedures so that generated data are valid, complete and reliable.

mappings.quote: The company should know their data life cycle and integrate the appropriate controls and procedures such that the data generated will be valid, complete and reliable.

requirements.item_text: Control and procedural changes for data integrity may address areas such as quality risk management, investigations, data review practices, computerised system validation, IT infrastructure, services and security, vendor and contractor management, training on data governance, handling of completed records (including cloud storage), oversight of purchasing critical equipment and IT with data integrity requirements, self-inspection covering data quality and integrity, and quality metrics reported to senior management.

mappings.quote: Specifically, such control and procedural changes may be in the following areas:  Quality Risk Management,  Investigation programs,  Data review practices (section 9),  Computerised system validation,  IT infrastructure, services and security (physical and virtual),  Vendor/contractor management,  Training program to include company’s approach to data governance and data governance SOPs,  Storage, processing, transfer and retrieval of completed records, including decentralised/cloud-based data storage, processing and transfer activities,  Appropriate oversight of the purchase of GMP/GDP critical equipment and IT infrastructure that incorporate requirements designed to meet data integrity expectations, e.g. User Requirement Specifications, (Refer section 9.2)  Self-inspection program to include data quality and integrity, and  Performance indicators (quality metrics) and reporting to senior management.

requirements.item_text: Where summary data are shared between sites of the same organisation, the supplying site's compliance may be evaluated by alternative means, such as evidence of following corporate procedures or internal audit reports.

mappings.quote: Where summary data is distributed between different sites of the same organisation, the evaluation of the supplying site’s compliance may be determined through alternative means (e.g. evidence of compliance with corporate procedures, internal audit reports, etc.).

requirements.item_text: The quality unit sets up a programme and schedule for ongoing audit trail reviews, based on each system's criticality and complexity, to verify current controls work and to detect potential non-compliance.

mappings.quote: The company’s quality unit should establish a program and schedule to conduct ongoing reviews of audit trails based upon their criticality and the system’s complexity in order to verify the effective implementation of current controls and to detect potential non-compliance issues.

requirements.item_text: Audit trail reviews are built into the company's self-inspection programme.

mappings.quote: These reviews should be incorporated into the company’s self-inspection programme.

requirements.item_text: Procedures exist to address and investigate audit trail discrepancies, including escalation to senior management and national authorities where necessary.

mappings.quote: Procedures should be in place to address and investigate any audit trail discrepancies, including escalation processes for the notification of senior management and national authorities where necessary.

requirements.item_text: Audit trail reviews include both random selections and targeted selections based on criticality or risk.

mappings.quote: Audit trail reviews should be both random (selected based on chance) and targeted (selected based on criticality or risk).

requirements.item_text: Data governance control strategies based on quality risk management principles are in place to prevent or mitigate risks.

mappings.quote: Data governance control strategies using quality risk management (QRM) principles (5) are required to prevent or mitigate risks.

requirements.item_text: The control strategy aims to put in place appropriate technical, organisational and procedural controls.

mappings.quote: The control strategy should aim to implement appropriate technical, organizational and procedural controls.

requirements.item_text: Controls may include procedures supporting data integrity compliance, a quality culture that encourages transparent reporting of failures with investigation and follow-up, controls that remove or reduce data risks to an acceptable level across the data life cycle, enough time and resources for a data integrity programme, monitoring through audits and self-inspections and continuous improvement, qualified and trained staff with regular GxP and data integrity training, validated computerised systems with the controls needed to protect electronic data, and defined roles and responsibilities for contract givers and acceptors in quality agreements and contracts with a focus on data integrity.

mappings.quote: Examples of controls may include, but are not limited to: ■■ the establishment and implementation of procedures that will facilitate compliance with data integrity requirements and expectations; ■■ the adoption of a quality culture within the company that encourages personnel to be transparent about failures, which includes a reporting mechanism inclusive of investigation and follow-up processes; ■■ the implementation of appropriate controls to eliminate or reduce risks to an acceptable level throughout the life cycle of the data; ■■ ensuring sufficient time and resources are available to implement and complete a data integrity programme; to monitor compliance with data integrity policies, procedures and processes through e.g. audits and self-inspections; and to facilitate continuous improvement of both; ■■ the assignment of qualified and trained personnel and provision of regular training for personnel in, for example, GxP, and the principles of data integrity in computerized systems and manual/ paper based systems; ■■ the implementation and validation of computerized systems appropriate for their intended use, including all relevant data integrity requirements in order to ensure that the computerized system has the necessary controls to protect the electronic data (3); and ■■ the definition and management of the appropriate roles and responsibilities for contract givers and contract acceptors, entered into quality agreements and contracts including a focus on data integrity requirements.

requirements.item_text: A system exists for regularly reviewing data for consistency with ALCOA+ principles, covering paper and electronic records in daily work and in system and facility audits and self-inspections.

mappings.quote: There should be a system for the regular review of data for consistency with ALCOA+ principles. This includes paper records and electronic records in day-to-day work, system and facility audits and self-inspections.

requirements.item_text: The effectiveness of implemented controls is evaluated, for example by tracking and trending data, reviewing data, metadata and audit trails (in areas such as warehouse and materials management, production, QC, case report forms and data processing), and routine audits and/or self-inspections that cover data integrity and computerised systems.

mappings.quote: The effectiveness of the controls implemented should be evaluated through, for example: ■■ the tracking and trending of data; ■■ a review of data, metadata and audit trails (e.g. in warehouse and material management, production, quality control, case report forms and data processing); and ■■ routine audits and/or self-inspections, including data integrity and computerized systems.
